title: The first result is only the beginning.
intro: A creator can describe a scene in a sentence. Directing it asks for something more precise: where a character moves, when they arrive, and what the camera sees.

I led the 3D Previs Stage from product definition to delivery inside MiniMax Design. The goal was to turn a creative intention into a visible, editable plan that could continue into the video workflow.

blocks.label: THE EDITING PROBLEM
blocks.text: “Keep the character’s movement. Just change the camera.”
blocks.note: Illustrative creator request, used to frame the design problem.

items.title: Space is hard to describe.
body: A prompt has to communicate distance, scale, blocking and framing all at once.

items.title: Timing changes the story.
body: The same movement can feel very different when an arrival, a camera move or a cut happens earlier.

items.title: A revision should stay local.
body: Regenerating a whole result can disturb choices that the creator already wants to keep.

I framed the first use cases around short films, advertising and product videos: tasks where a creator needs to rehearse a specific action and shot before committing to the final look. This was a product hypothesis shaped through prototypes and internal feedback.
